en.name: Za'atar
en.summary: Za'atar keeps about 6 months in an airtight jar in a dry, dark cupboard — the standard figure for a ground herb blend. A large tub is better sealed in the fridge, where roughly 1 year is a sensible working limit; that colder figure is our own extension of the rule for oily seeds, read across from sesame seeds, rather than a published number.
en.pantry: 6 months in an airtight jar, in a dry cupboard, out of sunlight and away from the heat of the stove. Za'atar is not a pure spice blend: the toasted sesame in it carries oil, and rancid sesame is what usually finishes an old jar — it tastes flat and faintly bitter well before it smells of anything. Buy small quantities. The dried thyme and the sumac both fade visibly, and a brown, dusty-looking za'atar has nothing left to give.
en.fridge: About 1 year sealed, which is worth doing for a large tub because it is the sesame oil you are protecting. Treat that as a working limit rather than a documented one — it comes from applying the general rule for oily seeds, and from the published keeping time for sesame seeds, to a blend that is mostly dried herb. Seal it well and let the jar warm to room temperature before opening so it does not take on condensation.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for za'atar. Freezing a sealed portion does protect the sesame oil, but the everyday cost is moisture: every trip out of the freezer invites condensation, and a damp blend cakes and loses its loose, sprinkleable texture. If you buy in bulk, freeze small sealed bags and keep one jar in use rather than reopening the same bag.
spoilage: A flat, faintly bitter taste — rancid sesame, and the usual way a jar dies.
Colour gone dusty brown, with none of the sumac's red or the herb's green.
Clumping or hard cakes, a sign moisture has got in.
Any visible mould, which means the jar goes out.
tips: Taste a pinch dry before you mix it with oil; rancidity shows on the tongue first.
Buy small; this is a blend you use up, not one you lay down.
Never dip a wet or oily spoon into the jar.
Za'atar already sold mixed with olive oil is a different product — it is not shelf-stable and belongs in the fridge.

faq.a: About 6 months airtight in a dry, dark cupboard. Sealed in the fridge, roughly 1 year is a reasonable working limit, though that figure is our own reading rather than a published one.

faq.q: How can you tell if za'atar has gone bad?
faq.a: Taste it dry. A flat, slightly bitter note means the sesame has gone rancid, which happens before any smell appears. Dusty brown colour means the thyme and sumac have faded.

faq.q: Does za'atar need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not a small jar you will finish in a few months. A large tub benefits, because the sesame oil is what limits its life. Za'atar pre-mixed with olive oil must be refrigerated.

zh.name: 扎塔香料
zh.summary: 扎塔香料裝密封罐、放乾燥避光的櫃子，大約可放 6 個月，這是乾燥香草粉類的一般標準。大罐的話密封冷藏比較好，抓 1 年是合理的工作上限；這個低溫數字是我們比照芝麻、把「含油種子要冷藏」這條通則延伸過來的，不是公布的數據。
zh.pantry: 密封罐、乾燥櫃子、避開日照與爐火的熱，6 個月。扎塔不是純香料粉：裡面的烤芝麻帶油，而一罐放久的扎塔通常就是被油耗的芝麻做掉的——它會先在味道上變得呆板、微苦，很久以後才聞得出味道。請少量買。乾燥百里香和鹽膚木粉的顏色都會明顯褪掉，一罐看起來灰褐、像灰塵的扎塔已經沒東西可以給了。
zh.fridge: 密封冷藏約 1 年，大罐才值得這樣做，因為你要保護的是芝麻的油脂。這要當成工作上限，不是有文件的數字——它來自把「含油種子」的通則和芝麻的保存期限，套到一個主體是乾燥香草的綜合香料上。密封好，開蓋前先讓罐子回到室溫，才不會結露受潮。
zh.freezer: 扎塔沒有公布的冷凍期限。密封小份冷凍確實能保護芝麻油脂，但日常代價是水氣：每進出冷凍一次就多一次結露，受潮的香料會結塊，失去那種可以隨手撒的鬆散感。真的大量採購的話，就分小袋密封冷凍，檯面上留一罐在用，不要一直開同一袋。
spoilage: 嚐起來呆板、帶點苦——芝麻油耗了，這是一罐扎塔最常見的死法。
顏色變成灰褐色，鹽膚木的紅和香草的綠都不見了。
結塊或結成硬塊，表示水氣跑進去了。
tips: 拌油之前先乾嚐一小撮；油耗會先在舌頭上現形。
少量買；這是一罐用來用完的香料，不是拿來囤的。
絕對不要把沾濕或沾油的湯匙伸進罐子。
已經調好橄欖油的扎塔是另一種產品，不能常溫久放，要冰冰箱。

faq.a: 密封放乾燥避光處大約 6 個月。密封冷藏的話抓 1 年是合理的上限，但那是我們的判斷，不是公布的數字。
乾嚐一小撮。呆板、微苦就是芝麻油耗了，這會比聞得出來更早發生。顏色變成灰褐則表示百里香和鹽膚木都褪光了。
幾個月內會用完的小罐不必。大罐有幫助，因為限制它壽命的是芝麻油脂。已經拌好橄欖油的扎塔則一定要冷藏。
